mcq.s: A rapid increase in the rate of inflation is sometimes attributed to the 'base effect'. What is 'base effect'?
o: It is the impact of drastic deficiency in supply due to failure of crops
It is the impact of the surge in demand due to rapid economic growth
It is the impact of the price levels of the previous year on the calculation of the inflation rate
None of the statements given above is correct in this context
mcq.x: Inflation is measured against last year's price level, so a low (or high) base in the previous year makes the current rate look high (or low): this is the base effect.

mcq.s: If the price index (base 1960 = 100) is nearly 330, it means that:
o: All items cost 3.3 times more than they did in 1960
The prices of certain selected items have gone up 3.3 times
The weighted mean of prices of certain items has increased 3.3 times
The price of gold has gone up 3.3 times
mcq.x: A price index is a weighted average of prices of a fixed basket of goods; an index of 330 on base 100 means that weighted mean has risen 3.3 times.

mcq.s: In the context of independent India's economy, which one of the following was the earliest event to take place?

Enactment of the Banking Regulation Act
Introduction of the First Five Year Plan
mcq.x: The Banking Regulation Act came in 1949; the First Plan began in 1951, SBI was formed in 1955 and life insurance was nationalised in 1956.

mcq.s: The difference between a bank and a Non-Banking Financial Institution (NBFI) is that:
o: A bank interacts directly with customers while an NBFI interacts only with banks and governments
A bank undertakes a range of financial activities with many kinds of customers, while an NBFI is mainly concerned with the term-loan needs of large enterprises
A bank deals with both internal and international customers while an NBFI deals only with external customers
A bank's main interest is to help business transactions while an NBFI's main interest is stabilising the currency
mcq.x: Banks accept deposits, give credit, clear cheques and serve a wide range of customers; NBFIs lack a full banking licence and mainly meet the term-loan needs of companies.
